findings.text: The fix is not live yet: commits `149fe5e63` (Processes.js) and `a91f41936` (server-guard.mjs + tests + docs) sit only on `worktree/runaway-search` — `git merge-base --is-ancestor worktree/runaway-search michael-dev-latest` (and `-local`/`-ref`/`-sync`) all say "no", and the branch has no upstream push. Servex itself (the long-running process whose `Processes.reap()` must gain the "burning" check) and any Bash/PowerShell session in the main checkout still run the old code, so the exact failure this task exists to stop — an orphaned recursive search burning a core after its shell is gone — is still unprotected right now. Nothing in the minion's reply to `mastermind-resources` (`inbox.jsonl`, 19:00:22) flags that a merge and a Servex restart are still needed before this does anything.

`server-guard.mjs`'s new `is_recursive()` can't distinguish a quoted literal pattern from a real flag: `tokens_of()` strips the quotes off `"-r"` before the recursive check runs, so `grep -n "-r" file.txt` (searching for the literal string `-r`, not recursing) reads as `-r` the flag and gets refused. This only over-blocks (fails toward safety, not risk), and isn't one of the test cases in either `BLOCK` or `ALLOW`, so it wasn't caught by the suite.
